prerequisites: It is recommended that the student has taken the courses "Fundamentals of Chemical Processes" and "Basic Operations I".

It is also recommended that students have basic knowledge of PVT properties of fluids, thermodynamic properties of pure fluids, thermodynamic properties in multicomponent systems and thermodynamics of phase equilibrium in solutions, knowledge acquired in the course "Chemical Thermodynamics applied to Engineering".

learning_outcomes.text: Design and calculate absorption operations by stages and continuously.
Design and calculate distillation and rectification operations.
Design and calculate liquid-liquid and solid-liquid extraction operations.
Design and calculate humidification, cooling, and solid drying operations.
Design and calculate adsorption and ion exchange operations.

syllabus_topics: Introduction to basic mass transfer operations. Basic and separation operations. Classification and fundamentals.
Rectification in plate columns: McCabe-Thiele method.
Rectification in plate columns: Ponchon-Savarit method.
Air conditioning operations: humidification and dehumidification.

assessment_methods.method: Partial assessment sessions (theoretical-practical questions and problems)

assessment_rules: For ordinary and extraordinary calls, the final grade is 80% final exam and 20% continuous assessment. The continuous assessment is divided into 10% for group tutorials (attendance and participation, 80% minimum attendance required), 30% for classroom practices (participation and Kahoot questionnaires), and 60% for partial assessment sessions (attendance and problem-solving, 80% minimum attendance required). The final exam requires at least 30% of the theoretical-practical part score and at least 30% of the problem-solving part score; the total final exam score cannot be less than 40% of its maximum value. For differentiated evaluation, the final grade is 100% based on a final exam. If a student does not have a continuous assessment score for extraordinary calls, a complementary assignment will be provided.
